requirements.requirement: Configure opsadmin on node1 for SSH access with the specified ed25519 public key
requirements.summary: opsadmin user was created (cmd-b452c31a32b0436c), the exact given public key was installed into ~/.ssh/authorized_keys with correct ownership and permissions (700/600) (cmd-71775431c1ed4d08), and the key content was verified byte-for-byte pre- and post-restart (cmd-412c1cea4cb54669, cmd-e97a4b55ef924a29). The account has no password (locked, shadow entry '!'), consistent with key-only access.

requirements.requirement: Require key-based SSH authentication (disable password/interactive auth) on node1
requirements.summary: A sshd_config.d drop-in enforcing PubkeyAuthentication yes / PasswordAuthentication no / KbdInteractiveAuthentication no / PermitEmptyPasswords no was written, validated (sshd -t), and activated via reload (cmd-bf85e74dc0a14cb2, cmd-605a25bff33a4465, cmd-f8f7d8c2d2cc4e8e). Effective config was independently confirmed with sshd -T (cmd-412c1cea4cb54669) and the sshd listener confirmed active (cmd-6bc028d22eff4e01). A live SSH attempt using only password auth was rejected with 'Permission denied (publickey)' both before and after a full node reboot (cmd-aee26dbe142e40af, cmd-e00968dfc25248b2), directly demonstrating enforcement and persistence.

overall_summary: The executor fully satisfied both material outcomes of the task: opsadmin was created with the exact specified ed25519 key installed with correct permissions, and SSH was restricted to key-based authentication via a validated, reloaded sshd_config.d drop-in, confirmed both by effective-config inspection (sshd -T) and by a live rejected password-authentication attempt. The executor additionally ran the independent node-restart evidence protocol, capturing a pre-restart baseline (boot_id, uptime, service/config state), a restart acknowledgement, polling through the outage, a changed post-restart boot_id, and full recovery of sshd, the opsadmin account, key permissions, and key-only enforcement — all cross-checked against the fixed before-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots, which show a boot_id change from ad55b012... to 69b3f677... consistent with the executor's own observations.
limitations: Only one managed node (node1) exists in this topology, so no cross-node comparison is possible.
A small residue file, /tmp/reboot.log, was left on the node after the reboot command and was not explicitly cleaned up (low-risk, non-security-relevant).
The 'ss' command was unavailable during one verification step, but the equivalent listening-socket check via netstat succeeded, so this does not reduce confidence in the SSH-listening evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor actions were tightly scoped to the task: user creation, key install, sshd drop-in, validation, reload, and read-only verification/testing. One minor missed step in cmd-bf85e74dc0a14cb2 wrote an unsupported 'UsePAM no' directive to the drop-in; this was immediately noticed and corrected in the very next command (cmd-605a25bff33a4465), leaving no bad residue in the final config. The backgrounded reboot command (cmd-59db047349c34f5f) left a small log file, /tmp/reboot.log, on the node (visible in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot) that was not cleaned up — a low-risk but unremoved residue. All other commands (discovery, sshd -T checks, netstat, boot-id/uptime polling during the outage, live SSH auth tests) were read-only and either succeeded or failed for benign/expected reasons (e.g., 'ss' binary absent, connection reset/timeout during the reboot window), none of which indicate unwanted state changes.
